description: A publisher sends one mention per remote reference in a newly published version: remote stub_of, remote transclusions entries, cross-origin forked_from. Same-origin references never send.
given: The thread T (remote transclusions), the stub S (remote stub_of) and the fork F (cross-origin forked_from).

expect.outcome: One mention per remote reference is enqueued with the correct relation; source is the item's absolute page and target is the target's absolute page.
asserts: A remote transclusions entry sends relation transclusion.
A remote blyg-target stub sends relation stub; a cross-origin fork sends relation fork.
source is the referencing item's absolute page and target is the target's absolute page; same-origin references send nothing.

description: Endpoint discovery: the target origin's manifest webmention key, else W3C discovery on the target URL (Link header, then HTML link/a), else no endpoint (recorded, not retried).
given: A target whose origin serves a manifest with a webmention key, and a target whose endpoint is only discoverable from its HTML.

expect.outcome: The manifest key wins when present; otherwise W3C discovery is attempted in order; if none is found the target is recorded as endpoint-less and not retried.
asserts: The manifest webmention key is consulted first.
W3C discovery then tries the Link header, then an HTML link/a element.
No endpoint is recorded as such and is not retried indefinitely.

description: Retry with backoff on network failure or 5xx; 4xx is terminal except 429; any 2xx counts as sent.
given: An outbound mention whose delivery returns a 5xx, then a 4xx, then a 429.

expect.outcome: 5xx is retried with backoff; 4xx is terminal; 429 is retried; any 2xx marks the mention sent.
asserts: Network failure and 5xx are retried with backoff.
4xx is terminal, except 429.
Any 2xx is recorded as sent.

description: Republish re-sends only for references that are new or whose target version changed.
given: A republished item whose references are unchanged, plus one whose target version advanced.

expect.outcome: Only the changed-target reference is re-sent; unchanged references are not re-sent.
asserts: New references are sent.
References whose target version changed are re-sent.
Unchanged references are not re-sent.

description: Withdrawal re-sends once for a withdrawn stub so the receiver marks the mention gone.
given: A stub that is later withdrawn (its endcap omits stub_of).

expect.outcome: Exactly one re-send is enqueued for the previously stubbed target.
asserts: A withdrawn stub re-sends once.
The re-send lets the receiver mark the mention gone.
The withdrawn endcap omits stub_of.

description: Delivery is fire-and-forget: publish MUST NOT block on it and outbound status is information, never a publish outcome.
given: A publish event with outbound mentions whose delivery is slow or failing.

expect.outcome: Publishing completes immediately; mention status is shown as information only.
asserts: Publish does not block on mention delivery.
Outbound status is informational.
A delivery failure never fails the publish.

description: The endpoint accepts POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded with source and target, returns 202, records the pair as pending, and verifies asynchronously; a re-sent pair re-verifies rather than duplicating.
given: A well-formed POST naming an absolute source and a target within this blyg's origin that names a published item.

expect.outcome: The endpoint returns 202, records the (source,target) pair as pending, and verifies asynchronously; a duplicate pair re-verifies instead of duplicating.
asserts: The request body is form-encoded with source and target.
Accept returns 202 and records the pair pending.
A re-sent pair re-verifies rather than creating a duplicate.

description: Syntactic checks return 400: both URLs absolute http(s); source != target; target within this blyg's own origin and naming a published item; unknown item is 400; a withdrawn target is accepted.
given: Malformed and out-of-scope POSTs: relative URL, source==target, foreign-origin target, unknown item id, and a withdrawn target.

expect.outcome: The malformed and out-of-scope cases return 400; the withdrawn target is accepted.
asserts: Both URLs must be absolute http(s) and source != target.
The target must be within this blyg's origin and name a published item.
An unknown item is 400; a withdrawn target is accepted.

description: Rate limits return 429: per source host, per coarser source group, and a global cap; a refused claim is never queued.
given: A burst of mentions from one source host, a wider source group, and a global flood.

expect.outcome: The applicable limit returns 429 and the refused claim is never queued.
asserts: Limits exist per source host, per coarser source group, and globally.
A refused claim returns 429 and is not queued.
Rate limiting keeps the verification queue finite.

description: Verification is bounded: at most 2 fetches (3 under 0.4 templates), at most 3 redirects, 5 seconds per fetch, 1 MB per body. These bounds are MUSTs.
given: A pending mention whose source must be fetched and possibly re-fetched via rel=alternate.

expect.outcome: Verification stays within the hard bounds and fails closed when they are exceeded.
asserts: At most 2 fetches (3 under 0.4 templates).
At most 3 redirects, 5 seconds per fetch, 1 MB per body.
The rate limit keeps the queue finite.

description: GET source: JSON with a blyg key is the item document; HTML is followed via rel=alternate application/json; anything else fails.
given: A source URL that returns HTML carrying <link rel="alternate" type="application/json">.

expect.outcome: The alternate JSON is fetched and used; JSON-with-blyg is accepted directly; any other content type fails.
asserts: JSON with a blyg key is the item document.
HTML is followed via rel=alternate application/json.
Anything else fails verification.

description: The item document's final URL must be exactly {origin}items/{id}.json for the document's own origin and id (normalized); a mirror copy never verifies.
given: A source document fetched from an origin/path other than its own {origin}items/{id}.json.

expect.outcome: Verification fails: the final URL does not match the document's own origin and id.
asserts: The final URL must equal {origin}items/{id}.json (normalized).
A mirrored copy fails verification.
Redirects do not excuse the mismatch.

description: A pinned version file never verifies a mention; only the canonical item document does.
given: A source URL pointing at items/{id}/v2.json rather than the canonical document.

expect.outcome: Verification fails because the final URL is not {origin}items/{id}.json.
asserts: A pinned version file never verifies a mention.
Only the canonical item document path verifies.
The mismatch is rejected regardless of content.

description: A source document with kind withdrawn is gone.
given: A verified source document whose kind is withdrawn.

expect.outcome: The mention is marked gone rather than verified.
asserts: kind=withdrawn is gone.
The mention record is kept and marked gone.
No content is stored.

description: Relation is stub when the source's stub_of names this blyg.
given: The stub S whose stub_of names the target item at this blyg.

expect.outcome: The mention verifies with relation stub.
asserts: A receiver believes a mention only when the fetched source names the target with a reference.
stub_of naming this blyg yields relation stub.
Identity members are compared; cited is ignored.

description: Relation is transclusion when a transclusions entry has this blyg as origin.
given: A source document with a transclusions entry whose origin is this blyg.

expect.outcome: The mention verifies with relation transclusion.
asserts: A transclusions entry originating at this blyg yields relation transclusion.
Only identity members are compared.
The entry's version is recorded.

description: Relation is fork when forked_from names a pinned version of the target.
given: The fork F whose forked_from names a pinned version of a target at this blyg.

expect.outcome: The mention verifies with relation fork.
asserts: forked_from naming a pinned version of the target yields relation fork.
The named version must be pinned.
cited is ignored in the comparison.

description: A forked_from naming an unpinned version does not verify a fork.
given: A source whose forked_from names a version that is not pinned at the target.

expect.outcome: Verification does not yield fork; without another matching reference it fails.
asserts: The referenced version must be pinned.
An unpinned reference does not verify a fork.
The relation order is stub, transclusion, fork, failed.

description: If no reference names this blyg, the relation is failed.
given: A source document that names this blyg nowhere (or only as text).

expect.outcome: The mention fails verification; no relation is recorded.
asserts: Relation order is stub, transclusion, fork, then failed.
Comparisons read identity members only and ignore cited.
A plain-text mention is not a structural reference.

description: On success the receiver records id/origin/version/kind/relation/author/page; NO content is stored.
given: A successfully verified mention.

expect.outcome: Only pointer metadata is stored; no content_md/content_html is retained.
asserts: The record holds id, origin, version, kind, relation, author and page.
No content is stored.
A verified mention is a pointer, not a copy.

description: A re-sent mention re-verifies and updates its record; a mention verified before that fails now becomes gone and the record is kept.
given: A previously verified mention whose source now fails to name the target.

expect.outcome: The re-verification flips the record to gone; the record is retained.
asserts: Re-sent mentions re-verify and update the record.
A previously verified mention that now fails becomes gone.
The record is kept, not deleted.

description: Verified mentions are studio signals: never auto-published, never in the feed/index/item documents; a publisher MAY display them only as per-item curation.
given: A blyg with verified inbound mentions on its items.

expect.outcome: Mentions appear only as per-item curation, never auto-published and never in any protocol surface.
asserts: Mentions are never auto-published.
They never appear in feed, index or item documents.
Any display is per-item curation only.

description: Plain (non-structural) mentions, if accepted, MUST be held apart from structurally verified mentions as a lower class.
given: A source that mentions the target without any structural reference.

expect.outcome: If accepted at all, a plain mention is stored as a lower class distinct from verified structural mentions.
asserts: Accepting plain mentions is a MAY; if accepted they are held apart.
Plain mentions are held apart from verified mentions.
They are never presented as structurally verified.

description: A static-only deployment advertises no endpoint, receives nothing, and remains fully conformant at every level.
given: A published blyg served entirely as static files, with no webmention key in its manifest.

expect.outcome: No endpoint is advertised, nothing is received, and the deployment is fully conformant.
asserts: The manifest omits the webmention key.
No receiving behaviour is required.
Static-only deployment is conformant at every level.
